14.evidence: Email is collected in three paths: (1) user-provided email during Supabase Auth sign-up/sign-in via index-BMHFFNQZ.js (supabase-js auth client sends email to Supabase Auth endpoint); (2) Google OAuth callback at api/auth/callback.js:34 (tokens.email passed to salvarToken()); (3) stored server-side via api/db.js:43-46 in user_tokens table. All paths are user-initiated (user chooses to sign up or connect Gmail). Destination is the developer's own Supabase/PostgreSQL backend (first party).
14.recommendation: Declare email collection in Play Store Data Safety form under 'App functionality' with user-initiated flag. No prominent in-app disclosure required since collection is user-initiated.

16.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection: Email data is sent via the backend email-service when the user explicitly triggers email sending. Disclosure exempt per Case 3, but EMAILS must be declared in the Play Store Data Safety form.
16.evidence: email-service/src/emailService.js lines 37-49: The enviarEmail function sends email data (subject line 'assunto', HTML body 'corpoHtml', recipient 'destinatario', sender name 'remetenteNome', PDF attachment) via Gmail SMTP. Routes defined in routes.js line 70-104 expose POST /enviar accepting userId, destinatario, assunto, corpoHtml, pdfBase64, pdfNome, remetenteNome — all transmitted to the developer's backend and then to Gmail. The user explicitly triggers this action (user fills form and clicks send).
16.recommendation: Declare EMAILS data collection in the Play Store Data Safety section under 'App functionality'. Since the user initiates the email sending (Case 3), prominent in-app disclosure is exempt, but the data type must be listed in the store listing's Data Safety form.

20.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32) despite all image handling being user-initiated single-file selection via <input type="file" accept="image/*"> — logo upload, stamp upload, and receipt scanning. TargetSdk=35 makes this a no-op on API 33+, but the broad storage permission is still in the manifest and is unnecessary since the WebView file chooser does not require it.
20.evidence: Manifest: READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 with maxSdkVersion=32. WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 with maxSdkVersion=28. requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11. Photo usage: SettingsModal.tsx:64 (logo upload, accept="image/*"), SettingsModal.tsx:134 (stamp upload, accept="image/*"), FinanceManager.tsx:267 (receipt scan, accept="image/*" capture="environment"). App is Biz-flow.cloud (business finance app), NOT a dedicated media manager.
20.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permissions from AndroidManifest.xml — the app's image selection flows use <input type="file"> which invokes the system file picker without requiring broad storage permissions on any modern Android version. Remove requestLegacyExternalStorage="true". No functional impact since all image operations are user-initiated and single-file.
